svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Sisukas course data architecture
svg.desc: System architecture of Sisukas course data. A daily GitHub Actions workflow (06:00 UTC) fetches course realisations from the Aalto Course API, transforms and validates them, reconciles them with the previously published catalogue, and publishes courses.json, historical.json and hash files to Google Cloud Storage, which is the authoritative canonical source. Separately, sisu-wrapper (FastAPI) queries SISU Kori and the Aalto Course API on demand to resolve missing courses and to return study groups and teaching events. The Node.js backend stores resolved course snapshots in PostgreSQL with a 180-day expiry; this storage is non-canonical. In the Svelte browser application, courses.json builds the active course index; historical.json builds a historical baseline; live snapshots from the backend are appended best-effort, duplicates are skipped and entries overlapping the active index are removed, producing an augmented historical index in memory without modifying any published dataset. The active view uses only the active index; the all-courses view merges active and augmented historical indexes with active records taking precedence. Curated curriculum, organisation and academic-period YAML is bundled at build time and loaded through separate loaders into filters. Study groups are fetched directly from sisu-wrapper into a separate study-group cache used by study-group, planning and schedule views.

g.text: Scheduled fetch, publication and download of the authoritative datasets
On-demand resolution, snapshots and study-group requests
Manually maintained YAML, loaded at build time (dashed)
Indexing, merging, de-duplication and consumption in memory
Arrowheads point where data moves. “Fetch / Download / Retrieve” labels: the receiving side starts the request.
Paired arrows show a request and its response separately. Badges (C R M P) repeat the colour meaning.
In-memory index produced by a stage
1 GCS is the only authoritative source of current and historical course data. IndexedDB copies, PostgreSQL snapshots and the study-group cache are derived or supplementary.
2 Runtime snapshots are never published to GCS or written into historical.json. They reach the browser only through the backend and only enter the in-memory historical index.
3 Active records take precedence: the pipeline enforces active ∩ historical = ∅ before publishing, and the browser prunes historical ids that overlap the active index.
4 Curated metadata and study groups use independent paths and never modify the course catalogue. Snapshot failures leave the canonical views working.
Implementation findings that differ from the brief
• Wrapper endpoints are /api/courses/resolve, /study-groups, /batch/study-groups and /batch/offerings; no /batch-resolve or /{id}/study-groups exists.
• Resolution uses SISU Kori to find CUR ids and the Aalto Course API for CUR payloads. The daily workflow uses only the Aalto Course API.
• The pipeline rejects duplicate ids rather than de-duplicating them. Curriculum YAML holds programme course lists; no credit-requirement rules were found.
• The backend resolve call uses a fixed window (2022-09-01 → 2025-12-31). Snapshot expiry is filtered by the backend; the browser checks payload completeness only.
• A newly resolved course appears in the browser after the next historical load. The sisu-wrapper historical crawl CLI is a manual tool and is not drawn here.
